blocks.tex: The retained analytic lemmas describe a regular level set using an implicit function and preserve open geometric constraints. Only the local analytic ingredients used by the regular-anchor construction are included.

blocks.label: def:collar_solution_data
blocks.title: Closed solutions and their strict interior
blocks.body:
Let \(D \subseteq X\) be a set of \emph{closed solutions} and \(U \subseteq D\)
its \emph{strict interior} (the solutions all of whose moderate-arc walls are
strictly satisfied).

blocks.label: thm:compact_collared_continuation
blocks.title: Compact collared continuation

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.compact_collared_continuation
lean.code:
theorem compact_collared_continuation
    {X K : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace K]
    [T2Space K] [PreconnectedSpace K]
    {D U : Set X} {π : X → K}
    (hD : IsCompact D) (hne : D.Nonempty) (hUD : U ⊆ D)
    (hπ : ContinuousOn π D)
    (hcollar : ∀ x ∈ D, ∃ y ∈ U, π y = π x)
    (hlocal : ∀ x ∈ U, π '' U ∈ 𝓝 (π x)) :
    π '' U = Set.univ := by
  exact closedImage_collared_continuation
    (hD.image_of_continuousOn hπ).isClosed hne hUD hcollar hlocal

blocks.tex:
The image \(\pi(D)\) is closed (compact image of a compact set under a map
continuous on \(D\)) and, by the local-openness hypothesis, \(\pi(U)\) is open.
The collar hypothesis gives \(\pi(D) = \pi(U)\), so \(\pi(U)\) is clopen and
nonempty in the preconnected space \(K\), hence all of \(K\).  This is exactly
\texttt{closedImage\_collared\_continuation} composed with the identifications
\(\pi(D)=\pi(U)\); see the Lean file for the two supporting lemmas
\texttt{fiberPurification\_iff\_image\_eq} and
\texttt{frontier\_subset\_iff\_eq\_univ}.

blocks.title: Discharging local openness: the fibrewise-submersion lemma

blocks.tex:
The local-openness input of \Cref{thm:compact_collared_continuation} is the one
analytic ingredient of the whole wiring, and it is \emph{not} the same statement
as the wall-crossing lemma below (which moves along a fibre at fixed parameter).
We state it first in the abstract form that the application consumes.

blocks.label: thm:regularWallZero_entersInterior
blocks.title: Regular wall zero enters the interior
blocks.body:
Let \(f : E \to F\) be a closure map with a surjective strict derivative \(f'\)
at a configuration \(a\), let \(w\) be an active wall functional with derivative
\(w'\), and let \(v \in \ker f'\) be a tangent direction that is strictly inward
for \(w\) (i.e.\ \(w'(v) > 0\)).  Then there is an exact level-set curve
\(\gamma\) with \(\gamma(0)=a\), \(\gamma'(0)=v\), staying on \(\{f = f(a)\}\) and
strictly increasing \(w\) for all small \(t>0\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.regularWallZero_entersInterior
lean.code:
theorem regularWallZero_entersInterior
    {E F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F]
    {f : E → F} {f' : E →L[ℝ] F} {a v : E}
    {w : E → ℝ} {w' : E →L[ℝ] ℝ}
    (hf : HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a)
    (hsurj : f'.range = ⊤)
    (hv : v ∈ f'.ker)
    (hw : HasFDerivAt w w' a)
    (hpos : 0 < w' v) :
    ∃ (γ : ℝ → E) (ε : ℝ),
      0 < ε ∧
      γ 0 = a ∧
      HasDerivAt γ v 0 ∧
      Tendsto γ (𝓝 0) (𝓝 a) ∧
      ∀ t, 0 < t → t < ε →
        f (γ t) = f a ∧ w a < w (γ t) := by
  let q : f'.ker := ⟨v, hv⟩
  let γ : ℝ → E := fun t =>
    hf.implicitFunction f f' hsurj (f a) (t • q)
  have hγ0 : γ 0 = a := by
    simp [γ, hf.implicitFunction_apply_image hsurj]
  have hq_deriv : HasStrictDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => t • q) q 0 := by
    simpa using ((hasStrictDerivAt_id (𝕜 := ℝ) (0 : ℝ)).smul_const q)
  have hq_tendsto : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t • q) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [ContinuousAt, zero_smul] using hq_deriv.hasDerivAt.continuousAt
  have hγ_tendsto : Tendsto γ (𝓝 0) (𝓝 a) := by
    simpa [γ] using
      (hf.tendsto_implicitFunction hsurj
        (g₁ := fun _ : ℝ => f a) (g₂ := fun t : ℝ => t • q)
        tendsto_const_nhds hq_tendsto)
  have hγ_deriv : HasDerivAt γ v 0 := by
    simpa [γ, q, Function.comp_def] using
      ((hf.to_implicitFunction hsurj).comp_hasStrictDerivAt_of_eq 0 hq_deriv (by simp)).hasDerivAt
  have hlevel : ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in 𝓝 0, f (γ t) = f a := by
    have hp : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (f a, t • q)) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 (f a, 0)) :=
      tendsto_const_nhds.prodMk_nhds hq_tendsto
    simpa [γ] using hp.eventually (hf.map_implicitFunction_eq hsurj)
  have hwall : HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => w (γ t)) (w' v) 0 := by
    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
      hw.comp_hasDerivAt_of_eq 0 hγ_deriv hγ0.symm
  have hslope :
      Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => t⁻¹ * (w (γ t) - w (γ 0)))
        (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (w' v)) := by
    simpa [smul_eq_mul] using hwall.tendsto_slope_zero_right
  have hgood :
      ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), f (γ t) = f a ∧ w a < w (γ t) := by
    filter_upwards [hlevel.filter_mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds,
      hslope.eventually_const_lt hpos, self_mem_nhdsWithin] with t hft hs ht
    refine ⟨hft, ?_⟩
    have hinv : 0 < t⁻¹ := inv_pos.mpr ht
    have hdiff : 0 < w (γ t) - w (γ 0) :=
      pos_of_mul_pos_right hs hinv.le
    rw [hγ0] at hdiff
    exact sub_pos.mp hdiff
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hεsub⟩ :=
    mem_nhdsGT_iff_exists_Ioo_subset.mp hgood
  refine ⟨γ, ε, hε, hγ0, hγ_deriv, hγ_tendsto, ?_⟩
  intro t ht0 htε
  -- … (truncated)

blocks.tex:
Proved in-tree via Mathlib's finite-dimensional implicit-function theorem
(\texttt{HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitFunction}); the level-set curve is
\(\gamma(t) = \mathrm{implicitFunction}(f(a), t\cdot q)\) with \(q = v \in \ker
f'\), and the strict inward slope follows from the derivative
\(\frac{d}{dt}\,w(\gamma(t))\big|_{0} = w'(v) > 0\).  See the Lean file; the
simultaneous multi-wall form is \texttt{regularWallZero\_entersAllInteriors}.

blocks.title: Joint submersion implies the projection image is a neighbourhood

blocks.tex:
The configuration space of the discrete problem carries two kinds of coordinate:
the \emph{parameter} (the curvature profile \(\kappa\)) and the \emph{fibre
variable} (the edge lengths \(\ell\)).  Solutions are the zero set of a closure
map \(G\), and the parameter map is a projection \(\pi\).  The statement we need
is that near a solution at which the \emph{pair} \((G,\pi)\) is a submersion, the
projection of the solution set covers a neighbourhood of the parameter.

blocks.label: lem:collar_proj_submersion
blocks.title: Joint submersion at a solution opens the parameter image
blocks.body:
Let \(E\) be a complete real normed space, \(F\) and \(K\) complete real normed
spaces, \(G : E \to F\), \(\pi : E \to K\), and let \(x \in E\) satisfy
\(G(x) = 0\).  Suppose \(G\) and \(\pi\) are strictly differentiable at \(x\)
with derivatives \(G'\) and \(\pi'\), and that the \emph{joint} derivative
\[
  v \;\longmapsto\; \bigl(G'(v),\,\pi'(v)\bigr) \;\in\; F \times K
\]
is surjective.  Let \(V\) be a neighbourhood of \(x\) and let \(U \subseteq E\)
be any set with \(\{G = 0\} \cap V \subseteq U\).  Then \(\pi(U)\) is a
neighbourhood of \(\pi(x)\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.projImage_mem_nhds_of_jointSubmersion
lean.code:
theorem projImage_mem_nhds_of_jointSubmersion
    {E F K : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace ℝ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    {G : E → F} {π : E → K} {G' : E →L[ℝ] F} {π' : E →L[ℝ] K} {x : E}
    (hGx : G x = 0)
    (hG : HasStrictFDerivAt G G' x) (hπ : HasStrictFDerivAt π π' x)
    (hsurj : (G'.prod π').range = ⊤)
    {V : Set E} (hV : V ∈ 𝓝 x)
    {U : Set E} (hU : {y | G y = 0} ∩ V ⊆ U) :
    π '' U ∈ 𝓝 (π x) := by
  have hH : HasStrictFDerivAt (fun y => (G y, π y)) (G'.prod π') x := hG.prodMk hπ
  have hmap : Filter.map (fun y => (G y, π y)) (𝓝 x) = 𝓝 (G x, π x) :=
    hH.map_nhds_eq_of_surj hsurj
  have hHV : (fun y => (G y, π y)) '' V ∈ 𝓝 ((0 : F), π x) := by
    rw [← hGx, ← hmap]
    exact Filter.image_mem_map hV
  have hWnhds : (fun k : K => ((0 : F), k)) ⁻¹' ((fun y => (G y, π y)) '' V)
      ∈ 𝓝 (π x) :=
    (continuous_const.prodMk continuous_id).continuousAt.preimage_mem_nhds hHV
  refine Filter.mem_of_superset hWnhds ?_
  rintro k hkW
  obtain ⟨y, hyV, hy⟩ := hkW
  have hyG : G y = 0 := (Prod.ext_iff.mp hy).1
  have hyπ : π y = k := (Prod.ext_iff.mp hy).2
  exact ⟨y, hU ⟨hyG, hyV⟩, hyπ⟩

blocks.tex:
Consider \(H := (G,\pi) : E \to F \times K\).  Its strict derivative at \(x\) is
\(v \mapsto (G'(v), \pi'(v))\), which is surjective by hypothesis, so the
inverse-function theorem in the surjective form (Mathlib's
\texttt{HasStrictFDerivAt.map\_nhds\_eq\_of\_surj}, the same step used in
Mathlib's Lagrange-multiplier proof) gives
\(H_*\,\mathcal N(x) = \mathcal N(H(x)) = \mathcal N(0, \pi(x))\).
In particular \(H(V)\) is a neighbourhood of \((0,\pi(x))\).

Let \(W := \{\,k \in K \mid (0,k) \in H(V)\,\}\); it is the preimage of the
neighbourhood \(H(V)\) under the continuous map \(k \mapsto (0,k)\) evaluated at
\(\pi(x)\), hence \(W\) is a neighbourhood of \(\pi(x)\).  If \(k \in W\), pick
\(y \in V\) with \(H(y) = (0,k)\); then \(G(y) = 0\) and \(\pi(y) = k\), so
\(y \in \{G=0\} \cap V \subseteq U\) and \(k \in \pi(U)\).  Thus
\(W \subseteq \pi(U)\) and \(\pi(U)\) is a neighbourhood of \(\pi(x)\).

blocks.label: lem:collar_hlocal_from_submersion
blocks.title: Interior submersion $\Rightarrow$ local openness
blocks.body:
Let \(U\) be a set of solutions of \(G = 0\) that is \emph{relatively open} among
solutions (every \(x \in U\) has a neighbourhood \(V_x\) with
\(\{G = 0\} \cap V_x \subseteq U\)) and at each of whose points the joint
derivative \((G',\pi')\) is surjective.  Then hypothesis~(4) of
\Cref{thm:compact_collared_continuation} holds: \(\pi(U) \in \mathcal N(\pi x)\)
for every \(x \in U\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.collar_hlocal_of_openSolutionSet
lean.code:
theorem collar_hlocal_of_openSolutionSet
    {E F K : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace ℝ K] [CompleteSpace K]
    {G : E → F} {π : E → K} {U : Set E}
    (hsol : ∀ x ∈ U, G x = 0)
    (hopen : ∀ x ∈ U, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, {y | G y = 0} ∩ V ⊆ U)
    (hreg : ∀ x ∈ U, ∃ (G' : E →L[ℝ] F) (π' : E →L[ℝ] K),
      HasStrictFDerivAt G G' x ∧ HasStrictFDerivAt π π' x ∧
      (G'.prod π').range = ⊤) :
    ∀ x ∈ U, π '' U ∈ 𝓝 (π x) := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨V, hV, hVU⟩ := hopen x hx
  obtain ⟨G', π', hG, hπ, hsurj⟩ := hreg x hx
  exact projImage_mem_nhds_of_jointSubmersion (hsol x hx) hG hπ hsurj hV hVU

blocks.tex:
Immediate from \Cref{lem:collar_proj_submersion} applied at each \(x \in U\)

blocks.label: def:collar_solution_sets
blocks.title: Configuration space, closure map, parameter projection
blocks.body:
Fix \(n \geq 3\).  A \emph{configuration} is a pair
\(p = (\kappa, \ell) \in (\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R}) \times
(\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R})\).  Define
\[
  G(p) \;=\; \bigl(\,\mathrm{closureGap}\,\kappa\,\ell,\;
                    \mathrm{turningSum}\,\kappa\,\ell - 2\pi \,\bigr)
  \;\in\; \mathbb{C} \times \mathbb{R},
  \qquad
  \pi(p) \;=\; \kappa .
\]
Thus \(G(p) = 0\) says exactly that the development of \((\kappa,\ell)\) closes
with total turning \(2\pi\), and \(\pi\) is the parameter (curvature-profile)
projection.  Given a set \(S\) of admissible profiles we write
\begin{align*}
  U &= \{\,p \;:\; \pi(p) \in S,\ \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell,\
        G(p) = 0\,\}, \\
  D &\supseteq U \quad\text{a compact set of closed configurations with
        saturated (\(\leq\)) moderate-arc walls.}
\end{align*}
\(U\) is the \emph{strict interior}: the moderate-arc predicate
\(\mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\) is an open condition
(\(0 < \ell_i\) and \(|\kappa_i|\,\ell_{i\pm}/2 < 1\)), so \(U\) is relatively
open among solutions, which is exactly the hypothesis of
\Cref{lem:collar_hlocal_from_submersion}.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.closureMapR3
lean.code:
noncomputable def closureMapR3 [NeZero n]
    (p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ)) : ℂ × ℝ :=
  (closureGap p.1 p.2, turningSum p.1 p.2 - 2 * Real.pi)

blocks.label: lem:collar_realizes_of_mem
blocks.title: Membership of \texorpdfstring{$U$}{U} gives realizability
blocks.body:
If \(n \geq 3\), \(p = (\kappa,\ell) \in U\) and \(\kappa_i > 0\) for all \(i\),
then \(\mathrm{RealizesR2}\,\kappa\).

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.realizesR2_of_mem_collarInterior
lean.code:
theorem realizesR2_of_mem_collarInterior [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    {S : Set (ZMod n → ℝ)} {p : (ZMod n → ℝ) × (ZMod n → ℝ)}
    (hp : p ∈ collarInterior S) (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < p.1 i) :
    RealizesR2 p.1 := by
  obtain ⟨-, hMA, hG⟩ := hp
  rw [closureMapR3, Prod.ext_iff] at hG
  have hE : closureGap p.1 p.2 = 0 := hG.1
  have hT : turningSum p.1 p.2 = 2 * Real.pi := by
    have h2 : turningSum p.1 p.2 - 2 * Real.pi = 0 := hG.2
    linarith
  exact ⟨p.2, hMA, hE, hT,
    isSimplePolygon_of_turningPositive hn hMA hpos hE hT⟩

deps.title: Configuration space, closure map, parameter projection
deps.label: def:collar_solution_sets

blocks.tex:
By definition of \(U\) the data \((\kappa,\ell)\) is moderate-arc, closes
(\(\mathrm{closureGap} = 0\)) and has total turning \(2\pi\).  Simplicity is
free in the positive case: all turning angles are positive, so the development
is convex, and \(\texttt{isSimplePolygon\_of\_turningPositive}\)
(\Cref{chap:discrete_convexity}) applies.  Unfolding
\(\mathrm{RealizesR2}\) with the witness \(\ell\) concludes.  This is the
Positive-Convexity Collapse: for positive profiles, realizability is exactly
closure existence.

blocks.title: Auxiliary declarations of the wiring file

blocks.tex:
The four blocks of this subsection record the supporting declarations that the
wiring theorem consumes.  They are elementary but load-bearing, and each carries
its own dependency edges.

blocks.label: def:collar_interior
blocks.title: The collar interior as a set
blocks.body:
For a chamber \(S\) of profiles,
\[
  \mathrm{collarInterior}(S)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\{\,p = (\kappa,\ell) \;\bigm|\;
     \kappa \in S,\ \ \mathrm{ModerateArc}\,0\,\kappa\,\ell,\ \
     G(p) = 0 \,\bigr\},
\]
the set \(U\) of \Cref{def:collar_solution_sets} written as a subset of
\((\mathbb{Z}/n \to \mathbb{R})^2\).
